## Overview
Bulk actions let you mark many activities complete, or move them to another owner, in one step.

## Before you start
- You need the `activities.bulk_update` permission. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager have it; Sales Representative and Viewer do not.
- **Reassign** is shown only to roles that may assign activities to others (Owner, Admin, Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Choose a tab: **All Activities**, **Tasks**, **Calls** or **Meetings**.
3. Click the **Grouped list** button next to the filters.
4. Click **Select**.
5. Tick the checkbox on each activity you want, or click **Select all** (shown with the number of loaded rows) to pick every loaded row.
6. Click **Mark complete**, or click **Reassign**.
7. If you chose **Reassign**, pick the **New owner** and click **Reassign**.

## Result
A message such as "5 of 5 updated" appears. Items that were already done, or already had that owner, are skipped.

## Tips
- Use the **View**, **Due** and search filters first so **Select all** picks only what you need.
- Click the **X** (**Stop selecting**) button to leave selection mode.
- Click **Table view** to return to the table.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Some selected activities are not yours to change. Nothing was updated."** Remove the activities you cannot edit and try again.
- **No Select button?** Your role does not have bulk actions.
articles.question: How do I mark several tasks complete or reassign them together?
articles.title: How to Complete or Reassign Many Activities at Once

## Overview
The **Calendar** tab shows your tasks, calls and meetings by month, week or day, including every occurrence of repeating meetings.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.view`. All built-in roles have it. A Sales Representative sees their own and their team's activities.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **Calendar** tab.
3. Choose **Month**, **Week** or **Day** at the top right.
4. Choose **My calendar** to see only your activities, or **Everyone** to see all activities you have access to.
5. Use the previous and next arrows to move through dates, or click **Today** to come back.
6. Click any event to open it.

## Result
The calendar shows each activity on its day. In week and day view, timed activities sit at their hour and all-day items appear in the **all day** row.

## Tips
- In month view, click **+N more** on a busy day, or click a day's date, to open that day.
- To schedule a meeting on a day, click the date of an empty day (month view) or double-click the day column (week or day view).
- Phones open the calendar in day view.
- You can also switch to the calendar from the table with the **Calendar view** button.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Could not load the calendar."** Click **Try again**.

articles.title: How to Use the Activities Calendar

## Overview
A task is a to-do with an optional due date and priority. Link it to a contact, company or deal so the next step is never forgotten.

## Before you start
- You need the `activities.create` permission. Owner, Admin, Sales Manager and Sales Representative have it; Viewer does not.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **New task** at the top right. (On another tab, click the arrow button next to the main button and choose **Task**.)
3. Type a **Title**, for example "Send the revised quote".
4. Optional: pick a **Due date** and a **Time**.
5. Optional: choose a **Priority** (**Low**, **Normal**, **High** or **Urgent**).
6. Optional: click **More details** to add a **Description** or link a **Contact**, **Company** or **Deal**.
7. Click **Create task**.

## Result
A "Task created" message appears and the task shows in the **All Activities** and **Tasks** tabs. A task with a due date also appears in **My Day** on that day, and in the **Overdue** card once it is late.

## Tips
- A title is enough. You can add the due date later with **Edit**.
- You can also create a task from any page with the **Create** button in the top bar, then **Task**.
- Turn on **Mark as done** under **More details** to record a task you already finished.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Pick a date for that time."** You entered a **Time** without a **Due date**. Pick a date or clear the time.
- **No New task button?** Your role cannot create activities. Ask an Admin to check your role under **Roles & Permissions**.

## Overview
Edit an activity to change its title, details, status or linked records. Delete it to remove it for everyone.

## Before you start
- Editing needs `activities.update` and deleting needs `activities.delete` for the activity. A Sales Representative can edit and delete their own activities; Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can change anyone's. Viewer can only view.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **⋮** actions button at the end of the activity's row.
3. To edit, click **Edit**.
4. Change the fields you need. Click **More details** for **Description**, **Contact**, **Company**, **Deal**, **Owner** and **Status**.
5. Click **Save changes**.
6. To delete instead, open the **⋮** menu again and click **Delete**.
7. In **Delete this activity?**, click **Delete**.

## Result
After saving you see an "updated" message. After deleting you see "Activity deleted" and the item is removed from lists, the calendar and the record's timeline.

## Tips
- Clicking the activity's title in the table also opens the edit form.
- Set **Status** to **Cancelled** to keep a record of an activity that will not happen, instead of deleting it.
- **Owner** is shown only to roles that can assign activities to others (Owner, Admin, Sales Manager).
- Deleting a repeating activity removes every occurrence.

## Troubleshooting
- **You see View instead of Edit?** You can only view this activity.

articles.title: How to Edit or Delete an Activity

The **Emails** tab on the Activities page lists the emails you can see: those sent from the CRM and replies synced from connected mailboxes, newest first.

## Before you start
- You need `email.view`. All built-in roles have it.
- Emails are sent and synced through a mailbox connected in **Settings** → **Communication** → **Email Settings**.

## Tips
- **Owner** shows who sent the email, or "Customer" for received emails.
- A red **failed** status means the email could not be sent.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No emails yet"** Nothing has been sent from the CRM yet, or no mailbox is connected.
- **No Emails tab?** Your role lacks `email.view`.

## Overview
The activity table lists tasks, calls and meetings with their related record, owner, due date and status. Filters above it narrow the list.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.view` (all built-in roles). A Sales Representative sees their own and their team's activities.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click a tab: **All Activities**, **Tasks**, **Calls**, **Meetings** or **Follow-ups**.

## Result
The table shows only matching rows, with columns **Activity**, **Related To**, **Owner**, **Due Date & Time** and **Status**. Click **Load more** at the bottom to see more rows.

## Tips
- Click a day in the small month calendar on the right to show only that day's activities.
- Filters are kept in the page address, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view.
- The **Grouped list** button shows the same activities grouped by **Overdue**, **Today**, **Tomorrow**, **Later**, **No date** and **Completed**, with a **Due** filter and a **Sort** list.

**Follow-ups** is a tab, not a separate activity type. It lists open activities that need a follow-up: calls logged with the outcome **Follow-up required**, and open tasks, calls or meetings whose title contains "follow" (for example "Follow up on quote").

- To add a follow-up, create a task with a title such as "Follow up with Priya", or log a call with the outcome **Follow-up required**.

## Overview
The top of the Activities page shows four summary tiles, and the right side shows schedule cards. Counts include every activity you are allowed to see.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.view` (all built-in roles).

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.

   - **Calls**: all calls, with the number this week.

Logging a call records a conversation that already took place, with its outcome and notes. The call is saved as completed.

## Tips
- On a contact or deal page, the **Call** quick action opens the same log form with the record already linked.

Mark a task, call or meeting as complete when it is done. Completed items move out of your open lists, and you can reopen them later.

- You need `activities.update` for the activity. A Sales Representative can complete their own activities; Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can complete anyone's.

- In the grouped list and in **My Day**, tick the checkbox at the left of a row to mark it as done.
- When you tick a call that has no outcome yet, a **How did the call go?** box opens. Pick an **Outcome**, add a **Note (optional)** and click **Mark as done**.
- A repeating task creates its next occurrence when you complete it.
- To complete many at once, see the bulk actions article.

**My Day** lists everything on your plate today: overdue items, today's tasks, events and calls, and tasks without a date. **Today's Schedule** on the right shows today's timed items as a timeline.

- You need `activities.view` (all built-in roles). My Day shows only your own activities.

2. Click the **My Day** tab.

- If nothing is planned, click **New task** in the empty My Day view to add one.
- The dashboard's **Today's Agenda** panel links here with **View all**.

## Overview
Tasks and meetings can repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Calls cannot repeat.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.create` for a new activity, or `activities.update` to change an existing one.
- A task must have a **Due date** before it can repeat.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **New task** (or open the arrow menu and choose **Meeting**), or click an existing task or meeting to edit it.
3. Fill in the **Title** and the **Due date** (task) or **Starts** (meeting).
4. Open the **Repeat** list and choose **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly** or **Yearly**.
5. In **Every**, enter how often, for example 2 for every two weeks.
6. For **Weekly**, click the weekday buttons to pick the days.
7. In the end list, choose **Never ends**, **Ends after** (then enter the number of times) or **Ends on** (then pick an end date).
8. Click **Create task**, **Schedule meeting** or **Save changes**.

## Result
The activity shows a repeat icon with a summary such as "Weekly on Mon, Wed". A repeating meeting appears on every matching day of the **Calendar**. A repeating task creates its next occurrence each time you complete it.

## Tips
- To stop a series, edit it and set **Repeat** to **Does not repeat**.
- Clicking one occurrence of a repeating meeting opens the meeting itself, so changes apply to the whole series.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Pick a due date to repeat this task."** Add a **Due date** first.
- **"Choose an end count or an end date, not both."** Pick only one end option.

articles.title: How to Make a Task or Meeting Repeat

## Overview
Rescheduling moves an activity to a new date or time. It uses the same edit form as **Edit**, so linked records, notes and attendees stay as they are.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.update` for the activity. A Sales Representative can reschedule their own activities; Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can reschedule anyone's.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Find the activity in the table.
3. Click the **⋮** actions button at the end of its row.
4. Click **Reschedule**.
5. Change the date and time:
   - Task: **Due date** and **Time**.
   - Call: **When**.
   - Meeting: **Starts** and **Ends** (or **Date** for an all-day meeting).
6. Click **Save changes**.

## Result
An "updated" message appears. The new date shows in the **Due Date & Time** column and on the **Calendar**. A meeting reminder moves with the new start time.

## Tips
- Rescheduling an overdue task to a future date removes it from the **Overdue** card.
- On the **Calendar** tab, click an event to open the same edit form.
- For a repeating meeting, changes apply to the whole series.

## Troubleshooting
- **"This activity was changed by someone else"** Click **Reload** in the form to load the latest version, then make your change again.

## Overview
Schedule a call you plan to make, so it shows in your list, on the calendar and in **Today's Schedule** on the day.

## Before you start
- You need the `activities.create` permission (Owner, Admin, Sales Manager, Sales Representative).

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **Calls** tab.
3. Click **New call**. (From any tab you can also click the arrow next to the main button and choose **Schedule call**.)
4. Enter a **Title**.
5. Set **When** to the date and time of the call.
6. Choose the **Direction**: **Outbound** or **Inbound**.
7. Optional: change **Duration (minutes)** (default 15).
8. Optional: type **Notes**.
9. Optional: click **More details** to link a **Contact**, **Company** or **Deal** and set a **Priority**.
10. Click **Schedule call**.

## Result
A "Call scheduled" message appears. The call is listed in the **Calls** tab and on the **Calendar**.

## Tips
- To record a call that already happened, use **Log a call** instead.
- When you later mark the call as done from the grouped list or **My Day**, you are asked how it went so the outcome is saved.
- Calls cannot repeat. For a regular check-in, schedule a repeating meeting or task.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Choose when the call happens."** The **When** field is required for calls.
- **"Enter 1 to 1440 minutes."** The duration must be a whole number of minutes, up to one day.

## Overview
A meeting is a calendar event with a start and end time, team attendees, a location or meeting link, and an optional reminder.

## Before you start
- You need the `activities.create` permission (Owner, Admin, Sales Manager, Sales Representative).

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **Meetings** tab.
3. Click **New meeting**.
4. Enter a **Title**.
5. Set **Starts** and **Ends**. For a full-day event, turn on **All day** and pick a **Date** instead.
6. Optional: add team members under **Attendees**.
7. Optional: enter a **Location** or a **Meeting link**.
8. Optional: choose a **Reminder** (default **30 minutes before**).
9. Optional: set **Repeat** for a recurring meeting.
10. Optional: click **More details** to add a **Description**, link a **Contact**, **Company** or **Deal**, or set a **Priority**.
11. Click **Schedule meeting**.

## Result
A "Meeting scheduled" message appears. The meeting shows on the **Calendar** and in the **Meetings** tab.

## Tips
- On the **Calendar** tab, click the date of an empty day (month view) or double-click a day column (week or day view) to start a meeting on that day.
- The meeting link must start with http:// or https://.

## Troubleshooting
- **"The meeting must end after it starts."** Set **Ends** later than **Starts**.
- **"Choose when the meeting starts."** **Starts** is required.

## Overview
A meeting can send you a notification before it starts. You set the reminder on the meeting form.

## Before you start
- To add a reminder to a new meeting you need `activities.create`. To change it on an existing meeting you need edit rights on that meeting (`activities.update`).
- Reminders are available for meetings only. The task and call forms have no reminder field.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **Meetings** tab.
3. Click **New meeting**, or click an existing meeting's title to edit it.
4. Open the **Reminder** list.
5. Choose **10 minutes before**, **30 minutes before**, **1 hour before** or **1 day before**. Choose **No reminder** to turn it off.
6. Click **Schedule meeting** for a new meeting, or **Save changes** for an existing one.

## Result
You get a notification at the chosen time before the meeting, as long as the meeting is still open.

## Tips
- New meetings default to **30 minutes before**.
- If you move the meeting, the reminder moves with it.
- Logged (past) meetings and calls never send reminders.
articles.question: How do I get a reminder before a meeting?
articles.title: How to Set a Reminder for a Meeting

## Overview
Subtasks split a task into smaller steps you can tick off one by one. The task shows progress such as 2/5.

## Before you start
- You need `activities.create` and edit rights on the parent task (`activities.update`).
- Only tasks can have subtasks, one level deep, up to 50 per task.

## Steps
1. Click **Activities** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **Tasks** tab.
3. Click the **Grouped list** button next to the search and filters.
4. Click the **⋯** actions button on the task's row.
5. Click **Add subtask**.
6. Type the step in **Add a subtask**.
7. Click **Add** (or press Enter). Repeat for more steps.

## Result
The subtasks appear under the task. A counter chip, for example 0/3, shows how many are done. Click the chip to show or hide the subtasks.

## Tips
- Tick a subtask's checkbox to mark it done; tick it again to reopen it.
- Subtasks also work in the **Activities** tab of a contact, company or deal.
- Click **Table view** to go back to the table.

## Troubleshooting
- **No Add subtask option?** It is shown only for top-level tasks you can edit. Calls, meetings and subtasks cannot have subtasks.
- **The add box disappeared?** The task already has 50 subtasks.
articles.question: How do I break a task into subtasks?
articles.title: How to Add Subtasks to a Task

The **WhatsApp** tab on the Activities page lists every WhatsApp message you can see, sent and received, newest first. It is a log; you reply from the contact's page.

The contact's page opens. Its **WhatsApp** tab shows the full conversation, where you can reply.

## Tips
- **Status** shows the delivery state, for example sent, delivered, read or failed.
- **Owner** shows who sent an outgoing message, or "Customer" for incoming ones.

- **"No WhatsApp messages yet"** Nothing has been sent or received yet, or WhatsApp is not connected.

## Overview
You send and reply to WhatsApp messages from a contact's **WhatsApp** tab. Free-text replies are allowed for 24 hours after the customer last wrote; outside that window you send an approved template.

## Before you start
- You need `whatsapp.send` (Owner, Admin, Sales Manager, Sales Representative).
- WhatsApp must be connected in **Settings** → **Communication** → **WhatsApp Integration**.
- The contact needs a phone number. Templates also need the contact's WhatsApp consent.

## Steps
1. Click **Contacts** in the left sidebar, then **People (Contacts)**.
2. Click the contact's name to open the record.
3. Click the **WhatsApp** tab.
4. If the window is open, type in **Write a reply…** and click **Send**.
5. If it shows **Window closed · templates only**, click **Send template message**.
6. Choose a **Template** and fill each **Value for {{1}}** box.
7. Click **Send template**.

## Result
"WhatsApp message queued" appears for template sends, and the message shows in the conversation. Ticks show **Sent**, **Delivered** and **Read** as the status updates.

## Tips
- Click **Templates and AI draft…** to open the full message box. If your role can use AI, pick a **Style** and click **Draft with AI**, then review the draft before sending.
- The **WhatsApp** quick action at the top of a contact page opens the same message box.

## Troubleshooting
- **"The 24-hour window has closed. Send an approved template instead."** Use **Send template message**.
- **"WhatsApp is not connected for this workspace"** Ask an Admin to connect it.
- **"No phone number"** Add a phone number to the contact.

## Overview
The WorkEasy AI Assistant answers questions about your customers, deals and activities using the CRM records you are allowed to see. It can also draft messages and suggest next steps.

## Before you start
- Your role needs AI Assistant access. Owner, Admin, Sales Manager, Sales Representative and Viewer all have it by default.

## Steps
1. Click **AI Assistant** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the box at the bottom that says **Ask anything… (e.g., create follow-up, write message, show report)**.
3. Type your question, for example "Which deals are at risk?" or "What did Acme say about pricing?".
4. Press **Enter** or click **Ask** (the arrow button).
5. Wait while it shows **Looking through your CRM…**.
6. Read the answer. To continue, type a follow-up question or click one of the suggestion buttons under the answer.

## Result
The answer appears as a chat bubble below your question. Follow-up questions keep the context of the conversation.

## Tips
- Good questions: "What should I follow up today?", "Summarize my pipeline.", "Show high-value deals closing this month.", "Catch me up on Acme".
- You can also click a suggestion under the chat, such as **Write a follow-up message**, **Show deal forecast** or **Team performance**.
- The assistant does not create or change records itself. Use **Create a task** or the create forms for that.

## Troubleshooting

Tell WorkEasy AI what to create, such as "Create a pipeline called Retail" or "Create a task to call ABC Corp", and it creates it for you. It can create pipelines, tasks, calls, meetings, deals, contacts, companies and tickets.

## Tips
- Name the record in your request, for example "Create a company Acme Corp". For a contact, add the email or phone number too.
- Say when it is due and WorkEasy AI sets the date.
- A new pipeline starts with the default set of stages. Change them under **Settings** → **Pipeline Stages**.

## Troubleshooting
- **It shows Review and create instead.** Something is missing, such as the name, or the day for a call or meeting. Click **Review and create**, fill in the form and save it.
- **It says your role can't create this.** Ask your workspace admin for the permission.

## Overview
The badge at the top right of the AI Assistant page shows how answers are produced. **Powered by AI** means the assistant writes full answers with analysis. **Knowledge search mode** means answers are assembled from your CRM records and conversations without AI-written analysis.

You know whether to expect **Analysis** in answers. In knowledge search mode you still get facts from your CRM, related records and sources.

## Tips
- The badge also shows **Knowledge search mode** when generative AI is switched off for the workspace in **Settings → AI Assistant → AI Settings**.
- Even under **Powered by AI**, a single answer can arrive without analysis. A note under the answer then explains why, for example an hourly or monthly AI limit, or a plan without AI answers.

## Troubleshooting
- **I always see Knowledge search mode.** Ask an administrator to check your role's AI permission and the workspace AI settings.
- **"…The information above was retrieved directly from your CRM."** AI writing was not available for that answer. The facts shown are still correct; try again later.

- **I cannot reopen an old conversation.** **Recent AI Actions** is a list of titles only. Your current conversation in the **Ask WorkEasy AI** panel is kept when you reload; older ones cannot be reopened.

## Overview
The lead score is a number from 0 to 100 shown next to a contact's status. It is a rules-based score, not a prediction: it adds and removes points for facts about the contact.

## Steps
1. Click **Contacts** in the left sidebar, then **People (Contacts)**.
2. Click the person's name to open the contact.

## Tips
- Points go up for: a later status (Prospect, Qualified, Customer), a complete profile (email, phone, company, job title), open or won deals, recent activity, a scheduled next activity, meetings, connected calls, email or WhatsApp replies, a larger company, and referral or website sources.
- Points go down for: Inactive status, a mostly empty profile, no activity for over 60 days, or never being contacted.
- Green means 70 or more, amber 40 to 69.

- **"Nothing has moved this score yet."** Log activities and link deals to raise it.

## Overview
A deal is a sales opportunity you track through a pipeline, from first contact to won or lost.

## Before you start
- You need `deals.create`. Owner, Admin, Sales Manager and Sales Representative have it; Viewer does not.
- At least one pipeline must exist.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. If you have several pipelines, select the pipeline the deal belongs to.
3. Click **Add Deal** at the right of the view tabs.
4. Type the **Deal name**.
5. In **Company**, type to search, or click **Create company** to add a new one.
6. In **Primary contact**, type to search, or click **Create contact** to add a new person.
7. Enter the **Amount** and check the **Currency**.
8. Set **Expected close**, **Priority** and **Source** if you know them.
9. Optionally add a **Description** and fill in **Additional Information**.
10. Click **Create deal**.

## Result
"Deal created" appears and the deal shows as a card in the first open stage of the selected pipeline. Its probability follows that stage.

## Tips
- If you can assign deals to others, choose the **Owner** at the top of the panel.

The AI assistant only works with CRM data the person asking can already see. Owners and Admins decide whether generative AI is allowed at all.

## Overview
WorkEasy is built so that your workspace's data is visible only to your own team, and only to the extent each person's role allows.

## Steps
1. Protect your own account: open **Settings → Security & Data → Password & 2FA** and click **Set up authenticator app**.

## Result
Your account needs both your password and a code from your phone to sign in.

## Tips
- **Separate workspaces.** Every workspace's data is kept apart and checked at the database level on every request, so one company can never see another company's records.
- **Role-based access.** What each member sees and changes is checked by the server on every request, not just hidden in the screen.
- **Extra confirmation.** Sensitive changes, such as role changes or removing a user, ask you to confirm with your password.
- **Encrypted connections.** The app is used over a secure (HTTPS) connection, and passwords and keys for connected apps are stored encrypted.
- **Audit trail.** Owners and Admins can review security-relevant changes in the **Activity / Audit Log**.
- **Nothing on your device.** The app does not keep CRM records on your phone or computer for offline use.
- **Two-factor for everyone.** Owners and Admins can require two-factor authentication for all members.

## Troubleshooting
- **I think someone else used my account.** Change your password, then click **Sign out other sessions** under **Active sessions**, and tell your Owner or Admin.

## Tips
- **Too many failed attempts.** After repeated wrong passwords, sign-in is blocked for a short while (up to about 15 minutes). Wait, then try again, or reset your password.
- **Forgot your password.** Use **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page.
- **Suspended or removed.** If your administrator suspended you, ask them to click **Reactivate**. If you were removed, ask them to invite you again.
- **Workeasy360 account.** Sign in with **Access WorkEasy CRM**; password and two-step problems are solved in Workeasy360.

## Troubleshooting
- **I lost my phone and have no recovery codes.** You cannot turn off two-factor authentication yourself without signing in. Contact support.
- **A banner says your organization requires two-factor authentication.** You are signed in, but must click **Set it up now** and set up an authenticator app before using the CRM.

Every action in WorkEasy is checked against your role. If your role does not allow it, you see a message such as "You do not have permission to perform this action." or a **No access** page, or the button simply does not appear.

- Common causes:
  - **Sales Representative** can edit, delete or move only records they own, and sees only their team's records.
  - **Viewer** is read-only.
  - Users, roles, the audit log and most settings are limited to the Owner and Admins.
  - Billing changes are limited to the Owner.

- When an Admin changes your role, you are signed out and get the new access when you sign in again.

## Troubleshooting

## Overview
Each plan includes limits, for example the number of records, team pipelines, automation rules, custom fields per module and monthly AI credits. Users are limited to the number of licences on paid plans.

## Steps
1. When an action is blocked by your plan, read the window that opens (**You've reached your plan limit** or **Upgrade to** a plan) and click **Compare plans** or **View add-ons**, or click **Not now** to close it.

## Result
Nothing you already have is deleted or changed. Only the action that would go over the limit is stopped, and the window tells you what is used against the limit.

## Tips
- Plan limits at a glance:
  - **Free**: 1 user, 500 records, 1 pipeline, 3 automation rules, no custom fields, no AI.
  - **Express**: 50,000 records, 3 pipelines, 30 automation rules, 10 custom fields per module.
  - **Premier**: 100,000 records, 5 pipelines, 50 automation rules, 25 custom fields per module, 1,000 AI credits a month.
  - **360**: 1,000,000 records, 15 pipelines, 100 automation rules, 50 custom fields per module, 3,000 AI credits a month.
- An add-on raises one limit without changing plan (paid plans only).
- The **Usage** meters on **Plan & usage** warn you before you hit a limit.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Your plan's user limit has been reached."** Remove a user, or have the Owner add licences.
- **The AI assistant stops writing answers.** Check **AI credits** on **Plan & usage**. If your workspace's monthly AI budget is reached, Ask WorkEasy keeps answering from your CRM records only, until next month.

The **?** icon in the top bar is the **Help** menu. It gives quick ways into search, the AI assistant and Settings.

## Steps
1. Click the **?** icon (**Help**) in the top bar, between the bell and your avatar.
2. Choose an option:
   - **Search everything** opens global search (shortcut **Ctrl K**).
   - **Ask WorkEasy AI** opens the assistant panel on the right.
   - **Help Center** opens the step-by-step guides for every feature.
   - **Settings** opens the Settings home page.

## Result
The chosen tool opens without leaving the page you are on (Settings opens its own page).

## Tips
- **Ask WorkEasy AI** only opens the panel if your role can use the AI Assistant.
- The **Settings** item is a shortcut; **Settings** is also at the bottom of the left sidebar.

## Overview
Sign in with the email and password you used when you created your account or accepted an invitation.

## Before you start
- You need a verified account. If you have not verified your email yet, open the link in the verification email first.
- If the page shows **Already a Workeasy360 user?**, your installation also offers Workeasy360 sign-in. Click **Use another sign-in method** to show the password form.

## Steps
1. Open the **Sign in** page.
2. Enter your **Email**.
3. Enter your **Password**.
4. Click **Sign in**.
5. If asked for an **Authentication code**, enter the code from your authenticator app and click **Verify**.

## Result
The CRM opens on the **Pipeline** page, or on the page you were trying to open before you signed in.

## Tips
- Forgot your password? Click **Forgot password?** under the password field.
- No account yet? Click **Create account** at the bottom of the form.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Verify your email" appears.** Your account exists but the email is not verified. Open the verification link we sent you, click **Back to sign in**, and sign in again.
- **"Sign-in is not available right now. Contact your administrator."** Password sign-in is turned off for this installation. Ask your administrator how to sign in.
- **Sign-in failed.** Check that Caps Lock is off and the email is spelled correctly, or reset your password.

## Overview
If two-factor authentication is on for your account, the CRM asks for a 6-digit code after your password. This keeps your account safe even if someone learns your password.

## Before you start
- Keep your authenticator app, or your saved recovery codes, at hand.

## Steps
1. Enter your **Email** and **Password** and click **Sign in**.
2. On the **Two-factor authentication** screen, open your authenticator app.
3. Type the current 6-digit code into **Authentication code**. You can type one of your recovery codes instead.
4. Click **Verify**.

## Result
You are signed in and the CRM opens.

## Tips
- Authenticator codes change every few seconds. If a code is about to expire, wait for the next one.
- To sign in as someone else, click **Use a different account**.

## Troubleshooting
- **"That code was not accepted."** Check that your phone's clock is set automatically, then try a fresh code.
- **I lost my phone.** Use a recovery code. If you have none left, ask an administrator for help.
- **A banner says your organization requires two-factor authentication.** Click **Set it up now** in the banner to open the Security page and turn it on.

## Overview
On phones and small tablets the CRM shows a bottom bar with the pages you use most, and the full sidebar moves into a slide-out menu.

## Steps
1. Use the bottom bar to jump to **Pipeline**, **Contacts** or **Activities**.
2. Tap **Search** to find any record.
3. Tap **New**, then choose **Task**, **Call**, **Contact** or **Deal** under **Create** to add a record.

## Result
You can work with the full CRM on a small screen, with your most common tasks one tap away.

## Tips
- The **Ask WorkEasy AI** button floats just above the bottom bar, so the assistant is always within reach.
- The bottom bar only shows **Search** and **New** if your role can search and create records.

## Overview
The left sidebar takes you to every part of the CRM, and the top bar holds search, the create menu, notifications, help and your account menu.

## Steps
1. Look at the left sidebar. It lists **Dashboard**, **Pipeline**, **Contacts**, **Activities**, **AI Assistant**, **Helpdesk**, **Products** and **Settings**.
2. Click any item to open that page. The current page is highlighted.
3. To reach people or companies, click **Contacts**, then choose **People (Contacts)** or **Companies** underneath it.
4. To hide or show those two sub-items, click the arrow next to **Contacts** (**Collapse Contacts** / **Expand Contacts**).
5. To return to the Dashboard from anywhere, click your workspace name and logo at the top of the sidebar.
6. Use the top bar on the right for **Create**, **Notifications**, **Help** (the **?** icon) and the **Account menu** (your avatar).

## Result
You can reach every page in one or two clicks. The sidebar also shows the **WorkEasy AI** card with an **Ask AI Now** button that opens the **Ask WorkEasy AI** panel.

## Tips
- Press **Ctrl K** (or **⌘ K** on a Mac) to search instead of browsing.
- If your role can use WhatsApp, a green **WhatsApp inbox** button in the top bar opens the WhatsApp tab of Activities.
- Administrative pages are inside **Settings**, not in the sidebar.

## Troubleshooting
- **I cannot see the sidebar.** On a small screen it is hidden. Tap **Open navigation** (the menu icon at the top left) to open it.

## Overview
The bell in the top bar collects reminders and alerts: tasks due, upcoming meetings and calls, deals assigned to you, inactive deals, customer replies, high-risk deals, integration alerts and automation messages.

## Steps
1. Look at the bell icon in the top bar. A red dot means you have unread notifications.
2. Click the bell to open **Notifications**.
3. Click a notification to open the record it is about. It is marked as read.
4. To clear the red dot, click **Mark all read**.
5. To choose which notifications you receive, click **Preferences** at the bottom of the list.

## Result
Unread items are shown in bold with a dot. When nothing is waiting you see **You're all caught up**.

## Tips
- The unread count refreshes about once a minute, and when you return to the browser tab.
- **Preferences** opens **Settings → Notifications**.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Notifications are unavailable right now."** Close the menu and open it again in a moment.
- **Clicking a notification does nothing.** Some notifications are not linked to a record; they are only marked as read.

## Overview
Create an account to start your own CRM workspace. You only need your name, email and a password; there is no separate company setup step.

## Before you start
- If a colleague invited you to an existing workspace, use the invitation link in your email instead. Signing up here creates a new, separate workspace.

## Steps
1. On the **Sign in** page, click **Create account** (next to **New here?**).
2. Enter your **Name**.
3. Enter your **Email**.
4. Enter a **Password** of at least 12 characters. Avoid common passwords and your name or email.
5. Click **Create account**.
6. On the **Check your email** screen, note the address the verification link was sent to.
7. Open that email and click the verification link.

## Result
After you verify your email, your workspace is created for you, with you as its Owner and a ready-to-use pipeline.

## Tips
- Already have an account? Click **Sign in** at the bottom of the form.

## Troubleshooting
- **The sign-up page sends me back to Sign in.** Accounts on this installation come from Workeasy360, so sign-up is closed. Use **Access WorkEasy CRM** on the Sign in page instead.
- **"Could not create your account."** Read the message under the field it mentions, for example an email that is already registered.

## Overview
If you are a member of more than one organization, you can move between them from the Account menu. Each organization's data is kept completely separate.

## Before you start
- The **Organization** section only appears when you have more than one active membership, for example after accepting an invitation from a second company.

## Steps
1. Click your avatar at the right end of the top bar to open the **Account menu**.
2. Find the **Organization** section. The workspace you are in now is selected.
3. Click the name of the organization you want to open.

## Result
The CRM reloads in the chosen organization and opens the **Pipeline** page. The top of the Account menu now shows that organization and your role in it.

## Tips
- Your role can differ between organizations, so menus and buttons may change after you switch.
- You can also switch from **Settings → Workspace → Organization Details**: in the **Your organizations** card, click **Open** next to an organization. The same card has **New organization** to create another workspace.

## Troubleshooting
- **I do not see an Organization section.** You belong to only one organization, or your other membership is not active yet.
- **"Could not switch organization."** Try again. If it keeps failing, your membership may have been disabled; contact that organization's administrator.

## Overview
Every ticket has one agent in **Assigned To**. A new ticket is assigned to the person who created it. Reassign it to move it to another agent's queue.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.update` with access to all tickets to assign them to someone else. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can do this. A Sales Representative can work on their own tickets but cannot hand them to another member.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the ticket's ID or subject in the list.
3. In the **Ticket Details** panel, click **More**.
4. Click **Reassign**.
5. Choose the agent in **Assign to**.
6. Click **Reassign**.

## Result
**Assigned To** shows the new agent, and the ticket appears in their queue straight away. The change is recorded in the ticket's **Activity** tab.

## Tips
- Use the **All Agents** filter, or choose **Me**, to see who has which tickets.
- The **Assigned To** column in the list shows **Unassigned** when no agent is set.

## Troubleshooting
- **"You cannot assign records to other members."** Your role can only keep tickets on yourself. Ask a Sales Manager or Admin to reassign it.

## Overview
A ticket records a customer's support request so your team can track it until it is resolved.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.create`. Owner, Admin, Sales Manager and Sales Representative have it; Viewer does not.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Create Ticket**.
3. Enter a **Subject**.
4. Choose a **Category**: **Technical**, **Billing**, **Account**, **Support**, **Sales** or **Other** (default **Support**).
5. Choose a **Priority**: **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Urgent** (default **Medium**).
6. In **Requester (contact)**, search for and pick the customer. If they are not a contact, type their name in **Or requester name**.
7. Optional: describe the problem in **Description**.
8. Click **Create Ticket**.

## Result
A "Ticket created" message appears with the ticket number (for example #TK-1044). The **Ticket Details** panel opens, and the ticket starts as **Open**, assigned to you.

## Tips
- You can also click **Create** in the top bar and choose **Ticket**.
- Link a contact if you want to reply by email or WhatsApp from the ticket.
- The **Description** becomes the first customer message in the **Conversation**.
- Priority sets the SLA deadline, so pick it carefully.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Subject is required."** Enter a subject before saving.
- **No Create Ticket button?** Your role cannot create tickets.

articles.title: How to Create a Support Ticket

## Overview
The Helpdesk list shows tickets with their ID, subject, customer, category, priority, status, agent and last update. Tabs, search and filters narrow it.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.view`. All built-in roles have it. A Sales Representative sees their own and their team's tickets.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click a tab: **All Tickets**, **Open**, **In Progress**, **Resolved** or **Overdue**. Each tab shows its count.
3. Type in **Search tickets by ID, subject, customer…**.
4. Optional: choose a priority in **All Priorities**.
5. Optional: choose a category in **All Categories**.
6. Optional: choose an agent in **All Agents**, or **Me**.
7. Optional: choose a product in **All Products**.

## Result
The list shows only matching tickets. Click **Load more** at the bottom to see more. Click a ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.

## Tips
- The **Resolved** tab includes closed tickets.
- The tiles at the top (**Open**, **In Progress**, **Resolved**, **Overdue**) also open their tab.
- **All Products** appears only if your role can view products.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No tickets match these filters"** Switch to **All Tickets**, reset each filter to its "All" option and clear the search.
- **"Helpdesk is not part of your role"** Ask an Admin to give your role access to tickets.

## Overview
Internal notes let your team share context on a ticket. They are visible to your team only and are never sent to the customer.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.update` for the ticket. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can add notes to any ticket; a Sales Representative can add notes to tickets assigned to them.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.
3. Click the **Internal Notes** tab.
4. Type your note in **Add an internal note…**.
5. Click the **Add note** button.

## Result
The note appears in the **Internal Notes** tab with a yellow background, your name and the time. The ticket's **Activity** tab records that a note was added.

## Tips
- Use notes to hand over a ticket before you reassign it.
- Notes do not change the ticket's status.

## Overview
Merge a duplicate ticket into the main one so the whole conversation is in one place. Delete a ticket only when it was created by mistake.

## Before you start
- Merging needs `tickets.update`. Deleting needs `tickets.delete`, which Owner, Admin and Sales Manager have. Sales Representative and Viewer cannot delete tickets.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the duplicate ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.
3. Click **More**.
4. Click **Merge into another ticket**.
5. In **Merge into ticket**, type the other ticket's number, for example #TK-1044.
6. Click **Merge**.
7. To delete a ticket instead, click **More**, then **Delete**.
8. Confirm with **Delete ticket**.

## Result
After a merge, the conversation moves to the other ticket, the duplicate is closed, and the main ticket opens. After a delete, the ticket and its conversation are removed for everyone.

## Tips
- Prefer merging or closing over deleting, so the history is kept.
- Deleting cannot be undone.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No other ticket has that number."** Check the number in the **Ticket ID** column and try again.

articles.title: How to Merge or Delete a Ticket

## Overview
Priority (**Low**, **Medium**, **High**, **Urgent**) decides how quickly a ticket must be resolved under the SLA. Category (**Technical**, **Billing**, **Account**, **Support**, **Sales**, **Other**) groups tickets by topic.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.update` for the ticket. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can change any ticket; a Sales Representative can change tickets assigned to them.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.
3. To change the category, open the **Category** list and pick a new one.
4. To change the priority, open the **Priority** list and pick a new one.

## Result
The change saves straight away and the list's **Category** and **Priority** columns update. A new priority also changes the ticket's **Due (SLA)** time.

## Tips
- You can also click **More** and pick a priority under **Change priority**.
- Raising a ticket to **Urgent** gives it the shortest SLA, so it may become **Overdue** sooner.

## Troubleshooting
- **The lists are read-only?** Your role can view this ticket but not change it.

articles.body:
## Overview
The **Conversation** tab of a ticket holds the messages between your team and the customer. You can log a reply, send it by email or WhatsApp, or record what the customer told you.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.update` for the ticket.
- To send by email you need `email.send` and a connected mailbox; by WhatsApp you need `whatsapp.send` and a connected WhatsApp account.
- Sending by email or WhatsApp needs the ticket to be linked to a contact with an email address or phone number.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.
3. Make sure the **Conversation** tab is selected.
4. Type your message in **Type your reply…**.
5. Open the **Send as** list and choose **Reply (log only)**, **Reply by email**, **Reply by WhatsApp** or **Log customer message**.
6. Click the **Send** button.

## Result
The message appears in the conversation. "Reply sent by email" or "Reply sent on WhatsApp" confirms an outgoing reply. The first reply to an **Open** ticket moves it to **In Progress**.

## Tips
- Click **Attach a file** to add a file to the ticket; see it under **Attachments**.
- Use **Insert emoji** for a quick emoji.
- WhatsApp free-text replies work only within 24 hours of the customer's last message.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Link the ticket to a contact to send replies."** The ticket has only a requester name. Use **Reply (log only)** or create the ticket for a contact.
- **"This contact has no email address."** Add an email address to the contact first.

## Overview
A ticket moves through **Open**, **In Progress**, **Resolved** and **Closed**. It becomes **In Progress** automatically when someone first replies. You resolve, close or reopen it yourself.

## Before you start
- You need `tickets.update` for the ticket. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can change any ticket; a Sales Representative can change tickets assigned to them.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the ticket's ID or subject to open **Ticket Details**.
3. Click **Mark as Resolved** at the bottom of the panel.
4. To close it instead, click **More** and then **Close**.
5. To open a resolved or closed ticket again, click **More** and then **Reopen**.

## Result
The status badge changes. Resolved and closed tickets are counted under the **Resolved** tab and no longer become overdue. A reopened ticket returns to **Open**.

## Tips
- To resolve several tickets at once, tick their checkboxes in the list and click **Mark as Resolved** in the bar that appears.
- From the list, the **⋮** actions button on a row also offers **Mark as Resolved**.

## Troubleshooting
- **Mark as Resolved is greyed out?** The ticket is already resolved or closed.
- **No buttons at the bottom of the panel?** Your role can only view this ticket.

articles.body:
## Overview
The resolution SLA sets how many hours a ticket of each priority may stay open before it counts as overdue. Defaults: **Urgent** 4 hours, **High** 8, **Medium** 24 and **Low** 72.

## Before you start
- Anyone with `tickets.view` can see the SLA. Only Owner and Admin (the `org.update` permission) can change it.

## Steps
1. Click **Helpdesk** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the **SLA settings** button next to the filters.
3. In **Resolution SLA**, enter the hours for **Urgent**, **High**, **Medium** and **Low** (1 to 2160).
4. Click **Save**.
5. To see late tickets, click the **Overdue** tab (or the **Overdue** tile).

## Result
"SLA updated" appears. The new hours apply at once to all open and in-progress tickets. Overdue tickets show a red **Overdue** label, and the ticket panel shows the **Due (SLA)** time.

## Tips
- The SLA clock starts when the ticket is created.
- Resolve or close a ticket to stop it from becoming overdue.
- The **Avg. Resolution** tile shows the average time to resolve over the last 30 days.

## Troubleshooting
- **Fields are greyed out with "Only workspace administrators can change the SLA."** Ask an Owner or Admin.
articles.question: How do I change the SLA hours for tickets?
articles.title: How to Set the SLA and Find Overdue Tickets

articles.body:
## Overview
Each stage becomes a column on the Kanban board. Add stages to match the steps of your sales process.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- A pipeline can have up to 30 stages.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline you want to change.
4. Click **Add stage** above the stages table.
5. Type the stage **Name**.
6. Choose its **Kind**: **Open**, **Won** or **Lost**.
7. Enter **Probability %** (0 to 100) for an open stage.
8. Pick a **Colour** and, optionally, type a **Description**.
9. Click the check mark button (**Save stage**).

## Result
"Stage added" appears and the stage is added at the end of the table. It shows as a new column on the board.

## Tips
- Choosing **Won** sets the probability to 100 and **Lost** sets it to 0; the field is locked for these kinds.
- Drag the new row or use its arrows to put it in the right place.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Duplicate stage name".** Two stages in one pipeline cannot share a name.
articles.question: How do I add a new stage to my pipeline?
articles.title: How to Add a Stage to a Pipeline

articles.body:
## Overview
The Analytics tab shows how the selected pipeline performs: how many deals move through each stage, how many are won or lost, where deals come from and how each owner is doing.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Analytics** in the view tabs.
3. Choose a pipeline in the **Pipeline** drop-down.
4. Optionally narrow the data with **Search deals…**, the owner filter (**All Owners**), the source filter (**All Sources**) or the product filter (**All Products**).

## Result
Four panels appear:
- **Conversion by stage**: deals that reached each stage, as a share of those that entered the first.
- **Win / loss**: every closed deal in this pipeline.
- **Deals by source**: where deals came from, and how many were won.
- **Owner performance**: deals, wins and revenue won per owner.

## Tips
- Click **Clear** to remove the filters.
- The **Win Rate** tile above the tabs uses deals closed in the last 30 days.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No pipeline to analyse yet."** Create a pipeline first.

## Overview
A stage you no longer use can be archived. It disappears from the stages table and from the Kanban board. Stages are archived, not permanently deleted.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- The stage must be empty: move its deals to another stage first.
- A pipeline must always keep at least one Open, one Won and one Lost stage.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline.
4. On the stage row, click the archive button (labelled "Archive" followed by the stage name).
5. Click **Archive stage** in the confirmation dialog.

## Result
"Stage archived" appears and the stage is removed from the table and the board.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Move the deals out of this stage first."** The stage still has deals. On the **Pipeline** page, drag them to another column, then try again.
- **The archive is refused for a Won or Lost stage.** It is the last one of its kind. Add another stage of that kind first.

## Overview
Each deal card on the Kanban board always shows the deal name, company or contact, amount, probability, owner and expected close date. You can add up to 8 extra deal fields, including custom fields, per pipeline.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline.
4. Scroll to the **Card layout** section below the stages.
5. Click the field chips you want to show. Selected chips are highlighted; click again to remove one.
6. Click **Save layout**.

## Result
"Card layout saved" appears. The chosen fields show on every card of that pipeline, each with its label.

- After 8 fields are selected, the other chips are disabled. Remove one to pick another.

## Overview
A pipeline is the ordered set of stages your deals move through. Create a separate pipeline for each sales process, for example new business, renewals or partnerships.

## Before you start
- You need the manage-pipelines permission (`pipelines.manage`). The Owner, Admin and Sales Manager roles have it.
- Your plan sets how many team pipelines you can have.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. Click **New pipeline** at the top right.
4. Type a name in **Pipeline name** (for example "Renewals").
5. In **Stages from**, choose a template. The text under it lists the stages it creates.
6. Click **Create pipeline**.

## Result
A "Pipeline created" message appears and the new pipeline is selected in the list on the left. Its stages appear in the table on the right, ready to edit. The first pipeline in a workspace becomes the default automatically.

## Tips
- Every template comes with a won stage and a lost stage. You can rename, add, reorder or archive stages afterwards.
- On the **Pipeline** page (wide screens) you can also click **Add pipeline** at the bottom of the **Pipelines** column. It opens this same settings page.

## Troubleshooting
- **"A pipeline with this name already exists."** Pipeline names must be unique. Choose another name.
- **The pipeline limit is reached.** Archive a pipeline you no longer use, or check your plan under **Settings → Billing & Subscription**. Sub-pipelines do not count towards the limit.

## Overview
The default pipeline is the one the **Pipeline** page opens with and the one new deals go to when no other pipeline is selected. Exactly one pipeline is the default.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- Sub-pipelines cannot be the default.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the **⋯** button next to the pipeline you want.
4. Click **Make default**.

## Result
A "Default pipeline updated" message appears and the **Default** badge moves to that pipeline. The **Pipeline** page now opens on it.

## Tips
- **Make default** is not shown for the pipeline that is already the default.
- To retire the current default pipeline, first make another one the default, then archive the old one.

## Overview
You can rename a pipeline at any time. When a pipeline is no longer needed, you archive it: it is hidden from the board but its history is kept. There is no permanent delete.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- To archive, the pipeline must not be the default, must have no open deals and no active sub-pipelines.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the **⋯** button next to the pipeline (its label is "Actions for" followed by the pipeline name).
4. To rename, click **Rename**, change **Pipeline name** and click **Save**.
5. To delete, click **Archive**, then click **Archive pipeline** in the confirmation dialog.

## Result
A rename shows "Pipeline renamed"; deals keep their stages and only the name changes. An archive shows "Pipeline archived" and the pipeline disappears from the board and the pipeline list.

## Troubleshooting
- **Archive is greyed out.** It is the default pipeline. Make another pipeline the default first.
- **"Could not archive pipeline".** Move or close (win or lose) its open deals, and archive its sub-pipelines first.
- **"This pipeline changed in the meantime."** Someone else edited it. Close the dialog and try again.

## Overview
Every stage has a name, a kind (Open, Won or Lost), a win probability, a colour and an optional description. The probability drives the weighted values on the board and in the forecast (value × probability).

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline.
4. In the stages table, click the pencil button on the stage row (labelled "Edit" followed by the stage name).
5. Change **Name**, **Kind**, **Probability %**, **Colour** or **Description**.
6. Click the check mark button (**Save stage**), or click **Cancel** (X) to discard.

## Result
"Stage updated" appears. The board shows the new name and colour. A deal that moves into the stage takes the stage's probability.

## Tips
- **Probability %** must be a whole number from 0 to 100. It can only be edited for **Open** stages; Won is always 100 and Lost is always 0.
- Renaming a stage does not move any deals.

## Troubleshooting
- **"A pipeline needs at least one won stage and one lost stage."** You cannot change the kind of the last Won or Lost stage. Add another one first.

## Overview
The filter row above the Kanban board narrows the cards to the deals you care about. The summary tiles and the Analytics tab follow the same search, owner, source and product filters.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Make sure **Kanban View** is selected.
3. Type part of a deal name in **Search deals…**.

5. Open the source filter (**All Sources**) and choose **WhatsApp**, **Facebook Ads**, **Website**, **Referral** or **Other**.

7. Open the status filter (**Any status**) and choose **Open**, **Won** or **Lost**.

## Result
Only matching deals stay on the board. Column counts and totals update to match.

## Tips
- Click **Clear** to remove all filters at once.
- Filters are kept in the page address, so a bookmarked link reopens the same filtered board.
- Save a combination you use often as a saved view.
- The product filter appears only if your role can see products.

## Troubleshooting
- **The board looks empty.** A filter is probably still on. Click **Clear**.

## Overview
The Forecast tab adds up open deals by their expected close date, weighted by probability (value × probability). It is arithmetic on today's pipeline, not a prediction.

## Before you start
- You need the Reports permission (`reports.view`). All standard roles have it; a Sales Representative sees team figures.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Forecast** in the view tabs.
3. Choose the **Period**: **This month**, **This quarter** or **Custom**. For **Custom**, set the **From** and **To** dates.
4. If you have several pipelines, choose one or keep **All pipelines**.
5. In **Group by**, choose **Stage**, **Salesperson**, **Team** or **Pipeline**.

## Result
Tiles show **Pipeline value**, **Weighted**, **Committed** (deals at or above the committed probability), **Won so far** and **Expected revenue** (weighted plus won). The **By month** panel and the breakdown table show the same figures per month and per group.

## Tips
- Click the **Pipeline value** or **Won so far** tile to open the matching deals in the List View.
- Deals without an expected close date are not in the forecast. Set a date on each open deal.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Forecast is not available for your role".** Ask an administrator for the Reports permission.
- **"Choose a date range".** With **Custom**, both dates are required.

## Overview
The Kanban view shows the selected pipeline as columns, one per stage, with a card for each deal. It is the default view of the **Pipeline** page.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Kanban View** in the view tabs.
3. Read each column header: the stage name, the number of deals, the total amount and, for open stages, the **Weighted** amount.
4. Read a card: deal name, company or contact, amount, probability, priority, owner, expected close date and the next activity.
5. Click a deal name to open the **Deal Details** panel.

## Result
You see where every deal stands and what each stage is worth.

## Tips
- A card with **No next step** has no scheduled activity. Plan one so the deal does not stall.
- A red close date means the expected close date has passed.
- Columns load up to 200 cards at first. Click **Show … more** at the bottom of a column to load the rest.
- Use the **Sort** drop-down to order cards by **Recently moved**, **Amount high–low**, **Closing soonest** or **Name A–Z**.
- The five tiles above the tabs show **Total Deals**, **Pipeline Value**, **Expected Revenue**, **Win Rate** and **Avg. Deal Cycle**, compared with the previous 30 days.

## Troubleshooting
- **"This pipeline has no active stages yet."** Add stages under **Settings → CRM Configuration → Pipelines & Stages**.

## Overview
The List View shows the deals of the selected pipeline as a sortable table. It is useful for scanning many deals, sorting by amount or close date, and finding archived deals.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **List View** in the view tabs.
3. Use the first drop-down to choose **All deals**, **My deals** or **Archived deals**.
4. Type in **Search deals…** to find a deal by name.
5. Pick an order in the **Sort** drop-down, for example **Closing soonest** or **Amount high–low**. You can also click a sortable column header.
6. Click a row to open the deal.

## Result
The table lists **Deal name**, **Stage**, **Company**, **Amount**, **Probability**, **Weighted**, **Expected close**, **Next activity**, **Owner** and **Status** (some columns appear only on wider screens). Clicking a row opens the full deal page.

## Tips
- Click **Filters** to filter by status (**Open**, **Won**, **Lost**) or by stage.
- When there are more deals than fit on one page, click **Load more** at the bottom of the table.
- The List View shows the pipeline selected on the **Kanban View**. To change pipeline, switch it there first.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No deals match these filters".** Click **Clear filters**.

articles.body:
## Overview
Besides Kanban and List, deals can be shown as a **Sheet** (edit cells like a spreadsheet), a **Calendar** (deals placed on a date) or a **Chart** (deals grouped and counted or summed).

## Before you start
- To change cells in the Sheet you need permission to edit those deals (`deals.update`).

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. In the small view switcher above the board, click **Sheet**, **Calendar** or **Chart**.
3. In **Sheet**: click a cell and type, or copy, paste and fill down (Ctrl+D). Click **Columns** to add, remove or reorder columns.
4. In **Sheet**: click **Save … rows** to save your edits, or **Discard** to undo them.
5. In **Calendar**: use **Previous month** and **Next month**, and choose the date field in **Place by** (expected close by default).
6. In **Chart**: choose **Count records** or **Sum of a field**, then choose the field to group by. Click **Show table** to see the numbers.

## Result
The deals of the selected pipeline appear in the chosen view. Sheet edits are saved together when you click save.

## Tips
- In **Calendar**, the **My events, tasks and calls** switch shows your own activities next to the deals.
- Save a view you use often with **Saved views**.

## Troubleshooting
- **A cell is marked and not saved.** You may only view that field, or someone else changed the deal first. Hover the cell to see why.

articles.title: How to Use the Sheet, Calendar and Chart Views for Deals

articles.body:
## Overview
The order of stages in settings is the order of the columns on the Kanban board, from left to right. Change it whenever your process changes.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline.
4. Drag a stage row by its handle to a new position, or click the up arrow (**Move … up**) or down arrow (**Move … down**) on the row.

## Result
The new order saves immediately, as the hint above the table says ("Changes save immediately"). The board columns follow the new order.

## Tips
- The up arrow is disabled on the first row and the down arrow on the last row.
- You cannot drag rows while a stage is being edited. Save or cancel the edit first.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Could not reorder stages".** The table returns to the saved order. Reload the page and try again.

articles.body:
## Overview
By default every member who can see deals sees every pipeline. You can restrict a pipeline so that only chosen teams and roles see it and its deals. Members who manage pipelines always see every pipeline.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- Create the teams first under **Settings → Workspace → Users & Teams**.
- Sub-pipelines follow their parent pipeline's access and cannot be restricted on their own.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the pipeline.
4. In the card below the stages, turn on the **Restrict to teams or roles** switch.
5. Under **Teams**, tick the teams that may use the pipeline.
6. Under **Roles**, tick the roles that may use it.
7. Click **Save access**.

## Result
"Access saved" appears and the pipeline shows a **Restricted** badge in settings and a lock icon in the **Pipelines** column of the Pipeline page. Members outside the chosen teams and roles no longer see it.

## Tips
- Turning the switch off makes the pipeline visible to everyone again.

## Troubleshooting
- **No teams are listed ("No teams yet.").** Create a team first, then return to this page.

articles.body:
## Overview
A saved view stores the current filters, columns, sort and view settings under a name, so you can reopen them in one click. You can keep it private or share it.

## Before you start
- Anyone can save private views. Sharing with others needs `views.share` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Set up the filters, sort and view (Kanban, List, Sheet and so on) you want.
3. Click **Saved views** above the board.
4. Click **Save as new view…**.
5. Type a **Name**.
6. If shown, choose **Who can use it**: **Only me**, **Everyone** or **Selected teams** (then tick the teams).
7. Optionally turn on **Open with this view by default**.
8. Click **Save view**.

## Result
"Saved" followed by the view name appears, and the **Saved views** button now shows the view's name. The view is listed in the **Saved views** menu.

## Tips
- To update a view you own, change the filters, open **Saved views** and click **Save changes to** the view.
- Use **Delete view** in the same menu to remove a view you own.
- **Stop opening with this view** removes it as your default.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Some of this view's fields are not available to you."** The view uses fields your role cannot see; those parts are left out.

## Overview
A sub-pipeline is a variant of a team pipeline with its own stages. It shares the parent's access rules and card layout, and does not count towards your plan's pipeline limit. Use it when one team sells in slightly different ways, for example online and field sales.

## Before you start
- You need `pipelines.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- A pipeline can have up to 10 sub-pipelines. A sub-pipeline cannot have sub-pipelines of its own.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Pipelines & Stages**.
3. In the list on the left, click the **⋯** button next to the parent pipeline.
4. Click **Add sub-pipeline**.
5. Type a **Pipeline name**.
6. Choose a template in **Stages from**.
7. Click **Create pipeline**.

## Result
The sub-pipeline appears indented under its parent. On the **Pipeline** board, buttons for the parent and its sub-pipelines appear above the columns so you can switch between them.

## Tips
- A sub-pipeline cannot be made the default pipeline.
- To change who sees it, change the access of the parent pipeline.

## Overview
When your workspace has more than one pipeline, the **Pipeline** page shows one pipeline at a time. It opens on the default pipeline, and you can switch at any time.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Make sure **Kanban View** is selected.
3. Open the **Pipeline** drop-down in the filter row (next to **Search deals…**).
4. Choose the pipeline you want.

## Result
The board, the summary tiles (**Total Deals**, **Pipeline Value** and so on) and the **List View** now show that pipeline's deals.

- On wide screens a **Pipelines** column on the left lists every pipeline. Click a name to switch. A lock icon marks restricted pipelines.

articles.body:
## Overview
Products are the items and services you sell, with their price and tax. Once a product exists, it can be added to deals as a line item.

## Before you start
- You need `products.create`. Owner and Admin have it; Sales Manager, Sales Representative and Viewer can only view products.

## Steps
1. Click **Products** in the left sidebar.
2. Click **Product** (with the plus icon) at the right of the toolbar. On an empty catalogue, click **Add product**.
3. Type the product **Name**.
4. Optionally type a **SKU**. It must be unique within your organisation.
5. Choose the **Status**: **Active** or **Inactive**.
6. Enter the **Unit price** and check the **Currency**.
7. Optionally enter **Tax rate (%)** and a **Tax label** such as GST or VAT.
8. Leave the **Stock** switch on if the item can be sold now.
9. Optionally add a **Description**.
10. Click **Create product**.

## Result
"Product created" appears and the product is listed on the **Products** page.

## Tips
- Prices are per unit, before tax. An empty unit price is saved as 0.
- Only **Active** products can be picked on a deal.
- To add many products at once, use **Import products** on the empty page, or **Settings → Security & Data → Import & Export Data**.

## Troubleshooting
- **An error on SKU.** Another product already uses that SKU. Use a different one.
- **No Product button.** Your role cannot create products. Ask an Admin.
articles.question: How do I add a new product or service?
articles.title: How to Add a Product

articles.body:
## Overview
Product lines turn a deal into a quote: each line has a product, quantity, price, discount and tax. The deal amount then becomes the total of the lines, tax included.

## Before you start
- You need `deals.update` for the deal. A Sales Representative can do this on their own deals.
- The deal must already be saved, and the product must exist and be **Active**.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the deal's name on its card, then click **Open full deal**.
3. Click the **Products** tab.
4. Click **Add product**.
5. Choose the product in **Product**. Its tax rate and, unless the deal uses a price book, its list price fill in.
6. Enter the **Quantity**.
7. Optionally change **Unit price**, **Discount (%)** or **Tax rate (%)**.
8. Click **Add product**.

## Result
"Product added" appears. The line is shown with its subtotal, tax and line total, and a **Total** row sums all lines. The deal amount updates to that total.

## Tips
- Click the pencil button on a line to change it, or the bin button and then **Remove** to delete it. The product itself is kept.
- Leave **Unit price** blank to use the list price, or the price book price if the deal uses one.
- Tax is charged on the discounted price.
- When all lines are removed, you can type the deal amount yourself again.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No active products."** Ask an Admin to add products or set them to **Active**.
- **The Add a product link in Deal Details opens the Overview tab.** Click the **Products** tab on the deal page.
articles.menu_path: Pipeline → Deal Details → Open full deal → Products
articles.question: How do I add products or line items to a deal?
articles.title: How to Add Products to a Deal

articles.body:
## Overview
You can change a product's name, price, tax or stock at any time. A product you no longer sell can be archived (deleted) and restored later.

## Before you start
- Editing needs `products.update`; archiving and restoring need `products.delete`. Owner and Admin have both.

## Steps
1. Click **Products** in the left sidebar.
2. Find the product, using **Search products…** if needed.
3. Click the **⋯** button at the end of its row (labelled "Actions for" followed by the product name).
4. To edit, click **Edit**, change the fields in **Edit product** and click **Save changes**.
5. To delete, click **Archive**.

## Result
An edit shows "Product updated". An archived product leaves the active list and shows an **Archived** badge.

## Tips
- To restore, choose **Archived products** in the first drop-down, open the row's **⋯** menu and click **Restore**.
- You can do the same from the product page: click **Edit**, or the **More actions** button for **Archive** or **Restore**.
- Setting **Status** to **Inactive** keeps the product but hides it from the deal product picker.
- Changing a product's price does not change deals that already include it.

## Troubleshooting
- **"This record was changed by someone else".** Click **Reload** in the form, then make your change again.
articles.question: How do I edit or delete a product?

articles.body:
## Overview
A price book is a named list of special prices for your products, in one currency. Use one for a customer group, a region or a currency. On a deal you can pick a price book so its prices are used instead of list prices.

## Before you start
- You need `pricebooks.manage`. Owner, Admin and Sales Manager have it.
- Add your products first.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Also in Settings** links under the cards, click **Price books**.
3. Click **New price book**.
4. Type a **Name**, for example "Wholesale".
5. Enter the **Currency** as a 3-letter code, for example INR.
6. Optionally type a **Description**.
7. Click **Create price book**.

## Result
"Price book created" appears and the book is listed with its currency, product count and **Active** status. Next, add prices to it.

## Tips
- The currency cannot be changed later. Create another price book for another currency.
- A deal can only use a price book in the deal's own currency.

## Troubleshooting
- **An error on Name.** Another price book already has this name.
articles.menu_path: Settings → Also in Settings → Price books
articles.question: How do I create a price book with special prices?
articles.title: How to Create a Price Book

articles.body:
## Overview
You can rename a price book, switch it off for a while, or archive it when it is no longer needed.

## Before you start
- You need `pricebooks.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Also in Settings** links, click **Price books**.
3. Click the **⋯** button on the price book's row (labelled "Actions for" followed by its name).
4. To rename, click **Edit**, change **Name** or **Description**, and click **Save changes**.
5. To switch it off or on, click **Deactivate** or **Activate**.
6. To remove it, click **Archive**, then **Archive** in the confirmation dialog.

## Result
The table shows the new name or the **Active** or **Inactive** status. An archived price book leaves the list.

## Tips
- Inactive and archived price books can no longer be picked on deals.
- Deals that already use an archived price book keep their prices.
- The currency of a price book cannot be edited.

articles.question: How do I deactivate or delete a price book?
articles.title: How to Edit, Deactivate or Archive a Price Book

articles.body:
## Overview
A price book holds one price per product. Products without a price in the book use their own list price.

## Before you start
- You need `pricebooks.manage` (Owner, Admin or Sales Manager). Other roles can see the prices but not change them.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Also in Settings** links, click **Price books**.
3. Click **Prices** on the price book's row.
4. In **Find product**, type a name or SKU.
5. Choose the product in **Product**.
6. Enter the **Price** in the book's currency.
7. Click **Add**.

## Result
The product appears in the **Prices in** card with its **List price** and **Price in book**.

## Tips
- To change a price, type the new value in **Price in book** and click **Save** next to it.
- To remove a product from the book, click the **X** button on its row (labelled "Remove" followed by the product name).
- Only active products appear in **Product**, and products already in the book are left out.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Enter a price like 99 or 99.50."** Use digits with up to two decimals, no currency symbol.
