## Overview
By default, product lines on a deal use each product's list price. Choose a price book on the deal to price its lines from that book instead.

## Before you start
- You need `deals.update` for the deal.
- An active price book in the same currency as the deal must exist.

## Steps
1. Click **Pipeline** in the left sidebar.
2. Click the deal's name on its card, then click **Open full deal**.
3. Click the **Products** tab.
4. Open the **Price book** drop-down next to **Add product** (it shows **List prices** by default).
5. Choose the price book.
6. Click **Add product** to add lines priced from the book.

## Result
The drop-down shows the chosen book. New lines with a blank **Unit price** take the price from the book; products not in the book use their list price.

## Tips
- Choose **List prices** to stop using the book.
- Members who cannot edit the deal see "Prices from" followed by the book name.

## Troubleshooting
- **No Price book drop-down.** There is no active price book in the deal's currency. Create one under **Settings → Price books**, or check the deal currency.

## Overview
The **AI policy** card controls what the assistant may do in your workspace. You can switch generative AI off completely and set a monthly spending budget.

The switch saves as soon as you change it, and the budget saves when you click **Save**. The text under **Monthly budget** shows the estimated spend this month and your limit.

## Overview
API keys let external software use the WorkEasy CRM API with only the permissions you grant. A key can never do more than the member who created it.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`integrations.manage`).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Integrations & API** card, click **API Keys**.
3. Click **Create API key**.
4. Type a **Name** after the system that will use it, for example "Accounting sync".
5. Under **Permissions**, tick only what it needs, for example **Read contacts** or **Create and update deals**.
6. Choose **Expires**: **After 30 days**, **After 90 days**, **After 180 days**, **After 365 days** or **Never expires**.
7. Click **Create key**.
8. If **Confirm it's you** appears, enter your **Password** and click **Confirm**.
9. Click **Copy** next to the **API key** and store it in a secret manager.
10. Click **I have saved it**.

## Result
"API key created" appears. The key is listed with its permissions, status, creator, expiry and **Last used** date. Only the start of the key is shown from now on.

## Tips
- To revoke a key, click **Revoke** on its row, then **Revoke key**. Systems using it lose access immediately; this cannot be undone.
- Send the key in the header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. Keys work only on the contacts, companies, deals and activities endpoints under `/api/v1/`.
- Create one key per external system so you can revoke one without affecting the others.

## Troubleshooting
- **Lost the key?** It cannot be shown again. Revoke it and create a new one.
- **"Choose at least one permission."** Tick at least one box.

## Overview
Automation rules run by themselves when something happens in the CRM, for example creating a follow-up task when a new lead is added. Rules act as the record's owner and never do more than the owner may do.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`automation.manage`). Sales Managers can view rules but not change them.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. Under **Also in Settings:**, click **Automation**.
3. Click **Create Automation**.
4. Type a **Name**.
5. Under **When**, choose the trigger: **A new contact (lead) is added**, **A new deal is created**, **A deal enters a stage**, **A deal is won** or **A deal is lost**.
6. If you chose **A deal enters a stage**, pick the **Stage**.
7. Under **Then**, choose **Create a follow-up task for the owner**, **Notify the owner**, **Notify the owner's team** or **Send a WhatsApp template to the contact**.
8. Type the **Task title** or **Notification text** (it defaults to the rule name).
9. Set the days in **Due after (days)** or **Wait before acting (days)**, from 0 to 90.
10. Optionally tick **Only if the contact has not replied**.
11. Click **Create**.

## Result
"Automation created" appears and the rule is listed, switched on, with "Has not run yet".

## Tips
- When you have no rules yet, click a ready-made rule to start: **New Lead Welcome (WhatsApp)**, **Follow-up Reminder**, **Proposal Follow-up** or **Deal Won Notification**.
- With **Only if the contact has not replied**, the step is skipped if the contact writes back on WhatsApp or by email during the wait.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Choose the stage the deal has to enter."** Pick a **Stage** for stage rules.
- **No Create Automation button?** Your role can only view automations.

## Overview
An automation can send an approved WhatsApp template to the contact, for example a welcome message when a new lead is added, or a reminder when a deal gets no reply.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`automation.manage`).
- WhatsApp must be connected and at least one approved template added in WhatsApp Integration.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. Under **Also in Settings:**, click **Automation**.
3. Click **Create Automation**.
4. Type a **Name**, for example "New lead welcome".
5. Under **When**, choose a trigger, for example **A new contact (lead) is added**.
6. Under **Then**, choose **Send a WhatsApp template to the contact**.
7. In **WhatsApp template**, choose an approved template.
8. Fill in each **Value for {{1}}**, **Value for {{2}}** and so on. You can use merge fields such as `{{first_name}}`, `{{company}}` or `{{owner_name}}`.
9. Optionally set **Wait before acting (days)** and tick **Only if the contact has not replied**.
10. Click **Create**.

## Result
"Automation created" appears. The rule shows the template name and, once triggered, how many times it ran and how many steps are waiting.

## Tips
- The message is sent from the record owner, and only to contacts who have agreed to WhatsApp messages.
- The ready-made **New Lead Welcome (WhatsApp)** and **Proposal Follow-up** rules open this editor so you can pick the template.

## Troubleshooting
- **"No approved WhatsApp templates yet."** Connect WhatsApp and add a template in Settings → WhatsApp.
- **"Fill in every template value."** Every numbered value needs text or a merge field.
- **"Last run skipped" under the rule?** The reason is shown, for example "The contact has no phone number." or "The owner may not send WhatsApp messages."

A member's role decides what they can see and do. Change it when someone's job changes, for example to make a Sales Representative a Sales Manager.

## Overview
Custom fields store your own information on Contacts, Companies, Deals and Products. A new field appears on the record form, in tables and in filters.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`customfields.manage`). Other roles can see custom fields but cannot create or change them.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **CRM Configuration** card, click **Custom Fields**.
3. Click the record type tab: **Contacts**, **Companies**, **Deals** or **Products**.
4. Click **New field**.

## Tips
- The key and type cannot be changed after the field is created. Choose them carefully.
- Available types: Text, Long text, Whole number, Number, Currency, Percent, Date, Date & time, Checkbox, Dropdown, Multi-select, Email, Phone and URL.
- A dropdown can have up to 100 unique options, each up to 100 characters.

## Troubleshooting
- **"A field with this key already exists for this record type."** Change the **Key** to a unique value.
- **Key error?** Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter, maximum 40 characters.

- The **Key** and **Type** are fixed once a field exists; only the label, options, help text and required setting can change.
- There is no permanent delete. Archive the field instead; you can restore it later with its stored values.
- Fields are listed by position. There is no option to reorder them on this page.

- **Button is greyed out with "Not configured for this workspace"?** An administrator must set the OAuth credentials on the server.

## Overview
Two-factor authentication asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (such as Google Authenticator, 1Password or Aegis) each time you sign in, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

## Before you start
- Install an authenticator app on your phone.

## Steps

6. Enter the 6-digit code from the app in **Confirmation code**.
7. Click **Enable two-factor**.

## Result
A message says **Two-factor authentication enabled**, the card shows **Enabled**, and your recovery codes appear. Save them somewhere safe.

## Tips
- To turn it off later, click **Disable two-factor**, then **Disable**. If your organization requires two-factor authentication, you lose access until you turn it on again.
- If you sign in with a Workeasy360 account, turn on two-step verification in Workeasy360. That is what your organization's requirement checks.

## Troubleshooting
- **"That code was not accepted."** Check that your phone's time is set automatically, then enter the newest code.

Export contacts, companies, deals or products to a CSV file, or everything at once as a ZIP with one CSV per module. Exports include every record you can see, with custom fields and tags.

- Owner, Admin and Sales Manager can export contacts, companies and deals. Products can be exported by Owner and Admin.

The file downloads to your computer. The **Export jobs** list shows when it was requested, the number of rows, the size and when it expires.

- Files are kept for 24 hours, then show "No longer available". Request a new export if needed.

## Overview
Rolling back an import deletes the records it created and restores the records it updated to their earlier values. Use it when a file was mapped wrongly or imported twice.

## Before you start
- You need permission to import that record type (for contacts: Owner, Admin or Sales Manager).
- You can roll back only your own imports, once, after they have finished (status **Completed**, **Stopped at limit** or **Failed**).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Security & Data** card, click **Import & Export Data**.
3. In **Import from CSV or Excel**, set **Record type** to the type you imported, for example **Contacts**.
4. In **Your recent imports**, find the file.
5. Click **Roll back** on its row.
6. Read the confirmation and click **Roll back**.

## Result
The status changes to **Rolling back**, then **Rolled back**. The row shows how many records were deleted, how many were restored and how many were left unchanged.

## Tips
- Records changed since the import, or that now have notes, files or links, are left as they are and listed so you can review them.
- You can also roll back from the import's progress view: click **View** on the row, then **Roll back**.

## Troubleshooting
- **No Roll back button?** The import is still running, was already rolled back, or was started by another member.
- **"This import was already rolled back."** Each import can be rolled back only once.

## Overview
The **Generic REST API** integration links WorkEasy CRM with any system that has a JSON REST API. After connecting, you choose which data it can see or change.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`integrations.manage`).
- Get the external system's base URL and credentials (API key, bearer token or OAuth 2.0 client details).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Integrations & API** card, click **Integrations (Connected Apps)**.
3. On the **Generic REST API** card, click **Connect**.
4. Type a **Name**, for example "Marketing platform".
5. Choose **Authentication**: **API key**, **Bearer token**, **OAuth 2.0 authorization code**, **OAuth 2.0 client credentials** or **Signed webhook only**.
6. Type the **Base URL**, for example `https://api.example.com/v1`.
7. Fill in the credentials: **API key**, **Bearer token**, or for OAuth the **Client ID**, **Client secret**, **Authorization URL**, **Token URL** and **Scopes**.
8. For OAuth, click **Copy redirect URI** and register that URI in the external system.
9. Click **Create connection**.
10. If **Confirm it's you** appears, enter your **Password** and click **Confirm**.
11. For **OAuth 2.0 authorization code**, click **Connect with OAuth** and sign in to the external system (or click **Later**).

## Result
"Connection created" appears and the connection's detail page opens. Credentials are stored encrypted and never shown again.

## Tips
- **Signed webhook only** creates a receive-only connection: enable its inbound webhook afterwards.
- Open **Advanced** only if the API does not follow common conventions (health check path, API key header, record ID field, list key).

## Troubleshooting
- **Name error?** Each connection needs a unique name.
- **"Could not start sign-in"?** The authorization URL must be a valid https address.

An inbound webhook lets the external system push contact, company and deal changes to WorkEasy CRM the moment they happen, instead of waiting for the next sync. Every request must be signed.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`integrations.manage`).
- The connection must be connected, and its data sharing set to **External → CRM** or **Two-way** for the record types it sends.

1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Integrations & API** card, click **Integrations (Connected Apps)**.

4. Click the **Inbound webhook** tab.
5. Click **Enable inbound webhook**.
6. If **Confirm it's you** appears, confirm your identity.
7. In the dialog, click **Copy** next to the **Webhook URL** and next to the **Signing secret**, and give both to the sending system's developer.
8. Click **I have saved it**.

## Result
The card shows an **Enabled** badge. The URL and secret are shown only once.

## Tips
- Supported event types are `contact.upsert`, `company.upsert` and `deal.upsert`. Only fields you mapped are applied.
- If the secret was lost or exposed, click **Rotate secret**; the old secret keeps working for 24 hours.
- If the URL was lost, click **Create new URL**, then **Create new URL** to confirm. The old URL stops working immediately.

## Troubleshooting
- **Enable button greyed out?** Reconnect the integration first.
- **Requests rejected?** Check the signature and that the timestamp is within 5 minutes of the current time.

Invite colleagues by email. They receive a secure link, create their own password and join your workspace with the role you choose. Administrators never see or set anyone's password.

The **Settings** page brings every administrative option together in six cards, so you can set up your workspace, team, communication channels, AI, security and integrations from one place.

2. Find the card for the area you want to change:
   - **Workspace**: **Organization Details**, **Users & Teams**, **Roles & Permissions**

   - **Communication**: **Email Settings**, **WhatsApp Integration**, **Message Templates**, **Notifications**

Remove a person when they no longer work with you. They lose access immediately, but the records they own and their history stay in the CRM.

## Overview
Every member has one role (called a profile on this page). WorkEasy has five built-in roles:
- **Owner**: full control, including billing and the organization itself.
- **Admin**: full data, user and settings management, but no billing.
- **Sales Manager**: works with all contacts, companies, deals, activities and tickets, including import and export; manages pipelines, price books and tags; shares views and dashboards; sees and exports reports; sends email and WhatsApp. Cannot manage users, roles, custom fields or the audit log.
- **Sales Representative**: sees their team's contacts, companies, deals, activities and tickets; creates new ones; edits, deletes and moves only their own; sends email and WhatsApp; sees team reports.
- **Viewer**: read-only access to records, reports and tickets.

## Before you start
- The Owner and Admins can open this page.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Workspace** card, click **Roles & Permissions**.
3. On the **Profiles** tab, click a role in the list.
4. Read each permission and its access level on the right.

## Result
You see exactly what the role allows. Access levels are **No access**, **Own records**, **Own + subordinates**, **Own team** and **All records**.

## Tips
- Built-in roles are marked **System** and cannot be changed. Create a custom profile from one to adjust it.
- The number next to each role is how many people have it.

## Troubleshooting
- **A colleague cannot see a record.** Check their role's access level here, and their team or place in the **Role hierarchy**.

## Overview
A webhook makes WorkEasy CRM send a signed HTTPS request to your endpoint the moment selected events happen, such as a new contact or a deal changing stage.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`webhooks.manage`).
- You need a public `https://` endpoint that can receive and verify the requests.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Integrations & API** card, click **Webhooks**.
3. Click **Add webhook**.
4. Type a **Name**, for example "Data warehouse".
5. Type the **Endpoint URL** (must start with `https://`).
6. Under **Events**, tick the events to send: **Contact created**, **Contact updated**, **Company created**, **Company updated**, **Deal created**, **Deal updated**, **Deal stage changed** or **Task completed**.
7. Turn on **Include record fields** only if the receiver needs the standard fields in the event itself.
8. Click **Create webhook**.
9. If **Confirm it's you** appears, enter your **Password** and click **Confirm**.
10. Click **Copy** next to the **Signing secret** and add it to the receiving system.
11. Click **I have saved it**.

## Result
"Webhook created" appears and the webhook is listed with its events, **Status**, **Last success** and **Last failure**.

## Tips
- With **Include record fields** off, events carry only the record type and ID; the receiver fetches details with an API key.
- The receiver should verify every request with the signing secret, as described in the signature headers shown in the dialog, and ignore repeated event IDs.
- Send a test from the **⋯** menu with **Send test event**.

## Troubleshooting
- **"Use a public https:// address."** Private network addresses and plain http are not allowed.
- **Lost the secret?** Use **Rotate secret** to get a new one.

## Overview
From the Webhooks list you can send a test event, see the latest deliveries, pause or resume a webhook, rotate its signing secret, or delete it.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`webhooks.manage`).

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Integrations & API** card, click **Webhooks**.
3. Click the **⋯** button on the webhook's row (labelled **Actions for** and the webhook name).
4. Click **Send test event** to check the endpoint.
5. Open the menu again and click **View deliveries** to see the latest 50 events with **Event**, **Status**, **Attempts**, **Response** and **Time**.
6. Use **Pause** or **Resume** to stop or restart sending.
7. Use **Rotate secret** to get a new signing secret, then copy it and click **I have saved it**.
8. Use **Delete**, then **Delete** to confirm, to remove the webhook.

## Result
You see "Test event delivered" with the endpoint's HTTP answer, or "Test event failed" with the reason. Other actions show "Webhook paused", "Webhook resumed" or "Webhook deleted".

## Tips
- Temporary failures are retried automatically.
- After rotating, WorkEasy signs with both the new and the previous secret for 24 hours, so switch the receiver over within that time.
- **Send test event** is available only while the webhook is active.

## Troubleshooting
- **Last failure shows an error?** The text explains it, for example "Only https:// addresses are allowed." or "The receiving system did not respond in time."
- **Deleted by mistake?** Deleting cannot be undone; create the webhook again.

## Overview
Connect one WhatsApp Business number to the workspace through the WhatsApp Business Cloud API. Everyone with WhatsApp permission then shares it, and conversations are kept on the customer's record.

## Before you start
- You need the Owner or Admin role (`whatsapp.manage`).
- Your plan must include WhatsApp integration (Express plan or higher).
- In Meta Business Manager you need a WhatsApp Business number set up for the Cloud API and a permanent system-user access token.

## Steps
1. In Meta Business Manager, open **WhatsApp → API setup** and copy the phone number ID, the WhatsApp Business account ID and your permanent system-user token.
2. In the CRM, click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
3. In the **Communication** card, click **WhatsApp Integration**.
4. In the **Business account** card, paste the number into **Phone number ID**.
5. Optionally paste the **Business account ID (optional)**.
6. Paste the token into **Access token**.
7. Click **Connect WhatsApp**.
8. If **Confirm it's you** appears, enter your **Password** and click **Confirm** (or click **Confirm with Workeasy360**).
9. Set up the webhook so replies reach the CRM (see the WhatsApp webhook article).

## Result
You see "WhatsApp connected". The card shows a **Connected** badge with the **Display name**, **Phone number**, **Phone number ID** and **Connected** date. The token is stored encrypted and never shown again.

## Tips
- On the Integrations page, **Manage** on the **WhatsApp Business** card also opens this page.

## Troubleshooting
- **"WhatsApp rejected the credentials"?** Meta did not accept the token or phone number ID. Copy them again from API setup.
- **"Meta phone number IDs contain digits only."** Paste the ID, not the phone number.
- **"...is not included in your plan"?** Upgrade in Billing & Subscription.
- **"Ask an administrator to connect the Business account."** Your role cannot connect WhatsApp.

## Overview
Meta delivers incoming WhatsApp messages and delivery receipts to the CRM through a webhook. Without it, customer replies do not appear and sent messages stay "Sent".

## Before you start
- WhatsApp must be connected (see the WhatsApp integration article).
- You need admin access to the app in Meta Business Manager.
- Your administrator must have set the verify token in the server configuration. The **Webhook** card shows **Configured** when the server side is ready.

## Steps
1. Click **Settings** in the left sidebar.
2. In the **Communication** card, click **WhatsApp Integration**.
3. In the **Webhook** card, click the copy button (**Copy webhook URL**) next to the address.
4. In Meta Business Manager, open **WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhooks**.
5. Paste the callback URL you copied.
6. Enter the verify token your administrator set in the server configuration.
7. Subscribe to the `messages` field.

## Result
Meta verifies the URL. Customer replies and delivery status (delivered, read) now appear on the contact's WhatsApp conversation in the CRM.

## Tips
- The webhook URL ends with `/api/v1/whatsapp/webhook/`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Badge says Not configured?** The server is missing the WhatsApp app secret or verify token. Ask your administrator to add them.
- **Messages stay "Sent" and replies do not appear?** The webhook is not verified yet, or the `messages` field is not subscribed in Meta.
- **"Copy failed"?** Select the URL and copy it manually.
